title: The 10 Best Corded Oscillating Tools
subtitle: Wired multi-tools ranked from live Amazon data — full power for flush cuts, plunge cuts, and scraping.
intro: An oscillating multi-tool vibrates a blade side to side thousands of times a minute to flush-cut trim, plunge-cut drywall, scrape caulk, and sand into corners. Corded models give you full, sustained power for the least money and never run out of charge — ideal for a workbench or long remodeling sessions. Amps are the thing to watch: around 3 amps and up cuts confidently, while sub-2-amp 'mini' tools stall on anything tough. Buy one that takes standard/universal blades so you're not locked into a brand's accessories.

products.name: AVID POWER 3.5-Amp Oscillating Multi-Tool (4.5° oscillation)
products.verdict: The best all-around corded multi-tool. A strong 3.5-amp motor, a wide 4.5° oscillation angle that cuts fast, variable speed, and tool-free blade change — all backed by nearly 4,000 reviews for around $50.

products.name: Hammerhead 2.2-Amp Oscillating Multi-Tool
products.verdict: The budget pick that punches above its price — a 2.2-amp corded tool with variable speed and 2,400 reviews at 4.5 stars for under $40. Fine for trim, drywall, and light remodeling.
pros: Simple and reliable for light work
cons: 2.2 amps is modest for heavy cutting

products.name: DEWALT 3-Amp Corded Oscillating Multi-Tool Kit
products.verdict: The pro's corded pick. A refined DEWALT with a dual-grip body, tool-free blade change, and a big accessory kit — 4.8 stars over 2,600 reviews. Expensive, but the one to buy if price is no object.
pros: Tool-free blade change, big accessory kit
cons: By far the most expensive here

products.name: CRAFTSMAN 3-Amp Corded Oscillating Multi-Tool
products.verdict: A solid name-brand corded tool with a universal tool-free accessory system and a 3-amp motor. CRAFTSMAN build at 4.7 stars, a step down in price from the DEWALT.

products.name: DEWALT DWE315SK 3-Amp Oscillating Multi-Tool Kit
products.verdict: The more affordable DEWALT corded kit. Same 3-amp DWE315 tool and tool-free blade change with a smaller accessory set and bag — real DEWALT for under $100.
cons: Smaller kit than the premium DEWALT

products.name: Dremel Multi-Max MM35 3.5-Amp Oscillating Tool Kit
products.verdict: Dremel more or less invented the consumer oscillating tool. The MM35 is a smooth 3.5-amp tool with a quick-change accessory system and universal blade fit — a safe, well-built pick.
cons: Pricier than the AVID for similar power

products.name: GALAX PRO 2.4-Amp Corded Oscillating Tool (28 accessories)
products.verdict: A big-value kit — a corded tool with 28 accessories and 2,600 reviews at 4.5 stars. The 2.4-amp motor is modest, but you get everything to start cutting for under $60.
cons: 2.4 amps is light for heavy cutting

products.name: ENERTWIST 4.2-Amp Oscillating Multi-Tool Kit (31 pieces)
products.verdict: The most powerful motor of the value kits — 4.2 amps with a 31-piece accessory set and 1,900 reviews. If you want corded muscle without paying DEWALT money, this is it.
cons: 4.4 stars, a hair below the leaders

products.name: WEN 3.5-Amp Oscillating Multi-Tool Kit
products.verdict: WEN's usual formula — real power for a low price. A 3.5-amp motor with variable speed and an accessory set for under $45, from a brand that specializes in value tools.
cons: Fewer reviews than the big kits

products.name: WORKPRO 3.0-Amp Corded Oscillating Multi-Tool Kit
products.verdict: A well-rounded 3-amp kit with seven variable speeds and a tool-free blade change. 925 reviews at 4.6 stars make it a safe mid-price choice.

avoid.name: NEWONE 1.8-Amp Oscillating Tool
avoid.flag: 1.8 amps — about half the motor of a real oscillating tool
avoid.verdict: At 1.8 amps this has roughly half the motor of a proper oscillating tool. It'll trim drywall and plastic, but it bogs down and overheats on the hardwood, nails, and grout you actually buy an oscillating tool to cut.
reasons: 1.8 amps is underpowered. The tools on this list run 2.2 to 4.2 amps; below about 2 amps, the blade stalls the moment you hit anything dense or a hidden nail.
It's a false economy — you'll save a few dollars over the Hammerhead or WEN, then fight the tool on every real cut and reach for something stronger.
For $5-10 more, the Hammerhead 2.2A or WEN 3.5A give you a genuinely capable tool with far more reviews behind them.
Buy on amps, not price: a weak oscillating tool is one you'll replace, not one you'll keep.

buyers_guide.a: A corded multi-tool gives you full, constant power for the least money and never runs flat — best for a workbench or long remodeling jobs. The trade is the cord and a wall outlet. Want to work anywhere? See the cordless list.

buyers_guide.q: How many amps do I need?
buyers_guide.a: Around 3 amps and up cuts confidently through wood, nails, and grout. 2 to 2.5 amps is fine for trim, drywall, and light work. Below about 2 amps, the tool stalls on anything tough — avoid the sub-2-amp 'mini' models.

buyers_guide.q: Do the blades fit any brand?
buyers_guide.a: Look for a 'universal' tool-free interface that accepts standard OIS/universal blades — nearly all the picks here do. Avoid tools that only take proprietary blades; you'll pay a premium for accessories forever.

It's how far the blade swings each stroke. A wider angle (around 3-4.5°) cuts faster and more aggressively; a narrower angle is smoother and more controlled. Some tools let you trade speed for control.
Yes. High speed cuts wood and metal fast; low speed keeps plastic and paint from melting and gives more control for detail work. Every pick above has it.
